Definition: from the same as G1759; hence (literally or figuratively); (repeated) on both sides:--(from) hence, on either side.
BiblicalUsage: Enteuthen is 'from hence' — from this place, or on either side. James asks where wars come from — hence, from our lusts, in James 4:1 — Jesus tells the traders to take these things hence in John 2:16, and the devil tells Him to cast Himself down from hence, from the pinnacle, in Luke 4:9. In Revelation the tree of life stands on either side of the river in Revelation 22:2.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'hence' is a word of direction — wars come from hence, from my own lusts, and the cleansing of the temple begins with taking these things hence. I hold that the tree of life standing on either side of the river is the end of the story: what was driven out is brought back, on both sides.
RelatedEvents: The Cleansing of the Temple; The Temptation in the Wilderness
